name: French Onion Pork Chops

fit.note: Published 406 cal / 14g carb clears the 400-650 cal and <=35g carb gate; 406 sits right on the 400 floor so a label-accurate recompute could dip under 400 - flagged for extract/map, but ruled on published numbers per instruction.

evidence: No catalog pork-chop recipe carries a French-onion profile (caramelized onions + beef stock + thyme + melted Swiss): the closest, 'southern-smothered-pork-chops-and-rice', is a cream-and-flour onion gravy served over rice with no beef stock or cheese, and 'creamy-mushroom-pork-chops', 'cheesy-pork-chop-and-hash-brown-casserole', 'no-peek-pork-chop-rice-casserole', 'marry-me-pork-chops' are all distinct sauce families - so this is not a duplicate of any live pork recipe.
cross_protein_flags: Structurally the SAME French-onion treatment (caramelized onion + beef broth + Swiss/gruyere) already lives in the catalog on OTHER proteins: 'slow-cooker-french-onion-chicken-bowls' (chicken) and 'slow-cooker-french-onion-pot-roast-bowls' (beef). Different protein AND different format (slow-cooker bowls vs seared skillet chops), so not a dupe under my scope, but the decider should weigh whether a third French-onion entry over-clusters that flavor family.

Also note a possible POOL collision I cannot fully adjudicate: another verdict file 'cheese-smothered-pork-chops.verdict.json' exists in this run's selected/ dir - a cheese-topped pork chop that could overlap the melted-Swiss angle; decider should compare the two pork-chop candidates head-to-head.
